key_insight: In the FAIR-ICI cohort, survival could extend well beyond immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment, while real-world survival was frequently less favorable than in pivotal trials.
clinical_relevance: Performance status was important when interpreting outcomes: ECOG ≥2 was associated with poorer overall survival than ECOG 0–1.
method: Retrospective cohort of 3,231 adults receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors across four Belgian hospitals.
Structured and unstructured electronic health records harmonized using OMOP-CDM and natural language processing.
Evaluated survival and treatment trajectories, with descriptive trial comparisons and multivariable Cox regression.
evidence_signal: Among 568 metastatic patients who discontinued ICIs without subsequent systemic therapy, median post-discontinuation survival was 21.4 months; ECOG ≥2 was associated with higher mortality across the analyzed cohort (adjusted HR 2.18, 95% CI 1.82–2.60).
watch_item: Retrospective observational data and descriptive trial comparisons cannot establish treatment effects or explain all differences between real-world and trial outcomes.
paper_title: Comprehensive real-world utilization, treatment trajectories, and outcomes of immune checkpoint inhibitors across cancer types: the multicenter FAIR-ICI cohort
